meta.method: WebSearch + WebFetch; PDF tables extracted locally with pypdf/PyMuPDF. Every number carries a URL and a date. Sites that blocked fetching (LoopNet, Census QuickFacts/API, NICB.org, Yelp, Cycle Trader, LADOT, SCAQMD, LADWP, TechTimes, Reddit and all Reddit mirrors) are flagged and their figures come from search-result snippets where used.
known_gaps: Reddit quotes (item 5) could not be retrieved: reddit.com, old.reddit.com, api.reddit.com, three redlib mirrors, and Bing/DuckDuckGo/Brave site:reddit.com queries were all blocked, captcha'd, or rate-limited (429). Section 5 says so explicitly rather than inventing quotes.
Google Trends is not fetchable (JS app); no keyword-volume tool was reachable. Proxies used instead: press coverage, Craigslist listing counts (LA vs SF Bay), MIC/MotorcyclesData unit sales.
DMV does not publish Class M license holders by county (or statewide) in either the county driver-license report or 'Statistics for Publication'.
CEC ZEV dashboard covers light-duty vehicles only; no public CA electric-motorcycle registration series was found.
768 Ceres zoning not shown on the listing mirrors that loaded; check ZIMAS before assuming retail sales are permitted.

registrations.source_note: CA DMV 'Estimated Vehicles Registered by County' is the DMV's county table (fee-paid registrations, calendar 2025). Statewide 2025: 763,800 fee-paid motorcycles (776,882 incl. fee-exempt), -3.0% vs 2024 (801,065). DMV 'Statistics for Publication' 2025 confirms 763,800 motorcycles = 2.3% of all vehicles.

Ventura.pop_note: ACS 2024 1-yr (Census Reporter) - DOF E-1 press-release attachment carried only the housing row for Ventura

la_county_most_motorcycles_of_any_us_cou.status: UNVERIFIED - plausible, not provable from public data found
la_county_most_motorcycles_of_any_us_cou.evidence: LA County = 133,368 (DMV 2025) / 139,137 (2024). IIHS (Polk VIN data, Jan 1 2023) state totals: CA 936,809; FL 668,046; OH 407,952; PA 403,039; TX 394,351; NY 370,101; IL 280,058; AZ 228,749. No cross-state county table was found. Maricopa County AZ (~62% of AZ pop) could hold ~140k if proportional, so LA is not certainly #1.

class_m_licenses.detail: DMV county driver-license report gives only total licenses outstanding (LA 6,772,857; SF 566,732; SD 2,475,208; Orange 2,413,906 as of Dec 31 2025). DMV Statistics for Publication breaks out only Commercial (Class A/B: 701,412) and Real ID, not Class M.

electric_motorcycle_registrations_ca.detail: CEC ZEV & Infrastructure Statistics track light-duty ZEVs only (BEV/PHEV/FCEV); motorcycles are not in the dashboard. CARB requires DMV verification for online/out-of-state ZEM purchases but publishes no counts. National proxy: MotorcyclesData reports US electric motorcycle sales YTD-2026 of 12,188 units (+24.8% y/y) vs +0.9% for the whole market.

registrations.key_observation: LA County has the largest absolute pool (133k) but the LOWEST per-capita rate of the 11 counties (13.5 per 1,000 residents) - below SF (18.9), Sacramento (18.6), Alameda (15.7). Ventura (26.4), Santa Barbara (24.9) and San Diego (24.1) are the highest per-capita counties; the 7 SoCal counties together (17.4/1,000) are essentially identical to the 4 NorCal counties (17.5/1,000).

car_dependence_and_commute.usc_2024_survey: 45% of LA County residents rely solely on a car (up from 33% in 2019); 23.8% used transit at least once in the past year (35.1% in 2019). https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/energy-efficient-car-dependent-the-state-of-mobility-and-sustainability-in-los-angeles/ (2024-08-16)
car_dependence_and_commute.freeway_share_of_commutes: NOT FOUND as a published statistic; proxy is the 2.3x higher drove-alone share in LA (64.8%) vs SF (28.6%). Average commute distance figure ('just under 9 miles', la.myneighborhooddata.org) appeared only in a search snippet and could not be verified on the page - treat as ESTIMATE.

lane_splitting.fact: Legal statewide since Jan 1, 2017 (AB 51, CVC 21658.1); California is the only US state that expressly permits it. CHP guidance: <=10 mph faster than traffic, discouraged above 30 mph.
lane_splitting.note: Applies equally in SF and LA - it is a California advantage, not a SoCal-only one; LA simply has far more freeway-miles and freeway commuters to exploit it.

hov_access.fact: Motorcycles are exempt from HOV occupancy requirements under CVC 21655.5 (Caltrans). Clean Air Vehicle decal solo access for EVs ended Sept 30, 2025 when federal 23 USC 166 authority expired - so a solo EV car driver lost HOV access but a solo FLASH rider keeps it.

weather.note: LA has half the rain days of SF; SF also has no real heat penalty (3 days >=90F).

motorcycle_culture.fact: LA County has the most registered motorcycles of any CA county (133,368, 2025) and the most motorcyclist fatalities (125 in 2023) and serious injuries (754).
motorcycle_culture.caveat: Per-capita ownership in LA (13.5/1,000) is BELOW SF (18.9/1,000) - see registrations.key_observation.

parking.note: Car parking is roughly 2x MORE expensive in SF than DTLA - this cuts AGAINST the founder's thesis on parking pain; LA's pain is congestion, not parking price.

gas_prices_aaa_2026_09_07.note: Record-high Labor Day prices statewide; SF ~10c higher than LA, so fuel savings argument is equal-or-slightly-stronger in SF.

scooter_maxi_scooter_market.context: MIC: scooters were the hardest-hit segment in 2025 as urban buyers moved to e-bikes; total new units 486,468 (-7.6%). Honda PCX 2026 MSRP $4,349; ADV160 $4,499. No state-level PCX/XMAX sales data is published.
scooter_maxi_scooter_market.note: Whole-US gas maxi-scooter market is only ~11k units/yr; the FLASH's addressable 'PCX/XMAX buyer' pool in CA is likely low thousands per year.

latino_working_class_market.note: 3x the Latino share and 35x the absolute Latino population of SF; lower incomes make a $4,799 vehicle a bigger share of income (financing matters).

apartment_dwellers_removable_battery.note: SF is actually MORE renter-heavy (61.8%) than LA (54.1%); the removable-battery advantage exists in both. No ACS 'no garage' variable found.

regulatory_tailwind.fact: LA City Council on 2026-08-25 unanimously ordered a 90-day report on regulating e-bikes/e-mopeds/e-motos, explicitly distinguishing illegal unregistered devices from street-legal, M1-licensed vehicles; SB 1167 (introduced Feb 2026, passed Senate Transportation 2026-04-07) bars selling mopeds/motorcycles labeled as e-bikes.
regulatory_tailwind.note: A DOT-certified, plated FLASH/Lightning is on the right side of this crackdown; grey-market Surron-class sellers are on the wrong side.

theft.riders_share_index_2022: Southern California rated 'Very High Risk' (highest state volume, year-round riding, port access); LA 600+/yr. https://www.riders-share.com/blog/article/motorcycle-theft-risk-index-usa
theft.rate_estimate: ESTIMATE: ~1,400 thefts / ~140k registered = ~1% of LA County motorcycles stolen per year; SF county-level count not found. Removable 3.3 kWh packs are themselves a theft target - store recommends indoor pack storage.

fatality_context.per_registered_estimate: ESTIMATE: LA 125 deaths / 139,137 regs (2024) = 0.90 per 1,000 registered; CA 583 / ~800k = 0.73 per 1,000.
fatality_context.judgment: A 299-lb, 75-mph hub-motor scooter with 13-14 in wheels riding in 70-80 mph LA freeway traffic is a different risk profile from SF surface streets; liability exposure and helmet/gear upsell should be planned.

sprawl_vs_range.flash_range: 70 mi tested (Electrek) / up to 106 mi claimed; dual 3.3 kWh packs
sprawl_vs_range.typical_socal_regional_trips: DTLA-Irvine 42 mi one-way (84 round trip), DTLA-Riverside 54 mi, DTLA-Ventura 68 mi - all beyond a safe freeway-speed round trip without a mid-day charge
sprawl_vs_range.judgment: Intra-basin commutes (<=20 mi each way) are fine; cross-county commutes need workplace charging (2 kW J1772 onboard charger is the selling point).

heat.inland_note: Valley/Inland Empire far hotter than downtown (no normals fetched).
heat.battery_effects: Vendor guidance: 5-10% temporary range loss above ~90-95F; sustained storage/charging above 95F accelerates irreversible capacity loss. Geotab fleet data (22,700 EVs): hot-climate vehicles degrade ~0.4 pct-points/yr faster; charging power matters more than climate.

insurance.electric_specific: Fewer carriers quote EVs; battery-damage total-loss risk raises comp/collision (Roamly). No 90021-specific quote obtainable without a VIN; ESTIMATE for a $5-6k FLASH in 90021: ~$250-450/yr liability-only, ~$700-1,100/yr full coverage (LA runs ~35% above CA avg).

listing.zoning: NOT SHOWN on mirrors - verify on ZIMAS (Warehouse District parcels are typically M2/M3; M2 generally permits retail but confirm)

site_768_ceres.judgment: Marketed as industrial 'Arts District & Downtown adjacent' near the 10 at Central Ave; the block is produce/wholesale warehouse and Skid Row-adjacent - no walk-in retail street. Treat it as a service/rental/battery-swap depot + destination showroom reached by appointment and paid demand generation, not a showroom that captures foot traffic. No foot-traffic data source found.

what_a_dealer_service_base_means.warranty_service: Field-swappable battery packs + hub motor mean most warranty work is module replacement; an 8,443-sf building with 26-ft clear and a grade door can hold 100+ crated units plus a 4-bay service area (JUDGMENT).
what_a_dealer_service_base_means.demo_events: Within a 2-hour van radius you can run weekend demo days in OC, IE, Ventura and (with an overnight) SB/SD; needs a trailer and 4-6 demo units (JUDGMENT).
what_a_dealer_service_base_means.freight: Crated e-moto LTL within SoCal is a 1-day lane from DTLA; no rate source fetched - ESTIMATE $150-300/unit LA->SD or LA->SB by LTL, far less than shipping from SF/Davis (~400 mi).

parking_rules_la_city.meters: NO free meter parking: LAMC 88.07/88.13 require immediate payment by any vehicle parked in a meter space; motorcycles are not exempt. https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-171368
parking_rules_la_city.sharing: LA City does not formally allow multiple motorcycles per paid metered space; some other CA cities do. https://www.infinitylawca.com/blog/moped-parking-laws-in-california
parking_rules_la_city.dtla_car_parking_benchmark: $160-200/mo (SpotAngels Sept 2026) vs SF $375-450 - the parking-cost argument is weaker in LA than in SF.

verdict: FACT - Absolute pool: SoCal's 7 counties hold 389k registered motorcycles vs 76k in SF/Alameda/Sacramento/Yolo (DMV 2025); LA County alone (133k) is 8.4x SF County (15.9k). Any fixed conversion rate yields far more FLASH buyers in SoCal.

FACT - But per-capita, LA is the WEAKEST motorcycle county in the set (13.5/1,000 residents vs SF 18.9, San Diego 24.1, Santa Barbara 24.9, Ventura 26.4), SoCal-7 and NorCal-4 aggregates are identical (~17.4/1,000), and LA registrations have fallen 19% since 2016. 'Motorcycle culture' is a volume story, not an intensity story.

FACT - Commuting structure favors SoCal: 64.8% of LA County workers drive alone vs 28.6% in SF (ACS 2024); lane splitting (CVC 21658.1) and solo HOV access (CVC 21655.5) are worth far more where the commute is a freeway. Solo-EV HOV decals died 2025-09-30; a plated FLASH keeps HOV access.
FACT - Weather: downtown LA has 34 rain days/yr vs 71 in SF and 26 days >=90F vs 3 - more riding days, but real heat-management needs for 3.3 kWh packs (store indoors, avoid charging hot).

FACT - Three founder assumptions do NOT hold: (a) car parking is ~2x cheaper in DTLA than downtown SF; (b) gas is ~10c/gal cheaper in LA; (c) the Bay Area has an e-moto purchase incentive (BAAQMD CC4A) and LA has none. Fuel/parking-pain arguments are at best equal to SF.

FACT - Risk is higher in LA: #1 US county for motorcycle theft (1,423 in 2018), 30% of US motorcycle thefts are in CA, LAPD motorized-device thefts +22% in 2024, 125 motorcyclist deaths in LA County in 2023, and full-coverage insurance ~$62/mo in LA vs $56 in SF.

ESTIMATE - Used-market proxy runs against the thesis: SF Bay Craigslist shows ~3-4x more used Zero/NIU/Surron listings than LA, implying a larger current installed base of electric two-wheelers in the Bay Area. LA is a bigger latent market, not yet a bigger actual one.

ESTIMATE - Sales potential: if the LA store matched 415 eBikes' ~40 vehicles/month and the SoCal motorcycle pool is 5x the NorCal pool, a mature LA store could plausibly run 60-120 vehicles/month, but the first 12 months are more likely 20-50/month because there is no HMP brand awareness or dealer in SoCal today, and two LA EV-only showrooms (Hollywood Electrics, EBC Newport) closed since 2024.

JUDGMENT - 768 Ceres is a good regional DEPOT (26-ft clear, 250A/480V for charging/swap, 1-2 hrs to OC/IE/Ventura, 2 hrs to SB/SD, $8k/mo is ~20% under list) but a poor SALES site: no walk-in retail, Skid Row-adjacent, produce-district traffic. Plan on appointment showroom + delivery + rentals + battery swap for DTLA couriers, and generate sales demand digitally and via demo days, not from the storefront.

JUDGMENT - Who buys a $5k 75-mph electric maxi-scooter: most likely a 25-45-year-old renter in the flat, dense, freeway-adjacent core (Koreatown / Mid-City / Hollywood / Silver Lake-Echo Park / DTLA / Culver City-Palms) with a 10-20 mi one-way commute, plus Westside tech/creative workers with workplace charging and OC/San Diego riders who already own scooters (highest per-capita). The Valley and Inland Empire skew to longer, hotter commutes that exceed comfortable freeway range; South LA/SE LA County is the delivery-rider Lightning MK.II + swap market. Sequence: (1) DTLA depot + rentals + swap, (2) digital sales + OC/Westside demo days, (3) SD/SB dealer support once the depot has parts and a service tech.
